Lexus Announces New Special Edition for the Best-Selling LBX Compact Crossover on the Old Continent
9 photos
Photo: Lexus
The premium Japanese automaker Lexus has revealed a special edition - it doesn't even carry a distinct name - for the LBX model, which is their best-selling model in the compact crossover SUV range.
The company hasn’t been very diligent when it comes to its European affairs: back in July, they showcased the Lexus LFA Concept at the 2026 Goodwood Festival of Speed with the world's first dynamic drives; early in September, they announced the “significant mid-lifecycle upgrade ” for the NX, and also launched the international sales of the Lexus LY680 luxury yacht – though the boat was actually exhibited at the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show in America.
Earlier this month, the brand also revealed the refreshed Lexus NX at the Nitto ATP Finals tournament in Turin, Italy, as a counterpoint to the “climax of the elite men’s international tennis season.” Lexus was a Platinum Partner and the Official Automotive Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals for the fourth year in a row, which is why the Lexus NX enjoyed a high-profile European reveal at the Nitto ATP Finals, which finished on November 22.
Now, the company is moving down the lineup to the subcompact luxury crossover SUV , with the B-segment LBX , primarily developed for Japan and Europe and offered since the 2024 model year, showcasing the first details for the model’s new special edition. The regular Lexus LBX is offered on the TNGA-B architecture shared with the Toyota Yaris Cross and has both ICE and hybrid versions.
The Lexus brand says the LBX has quickly become its best-selling model in Europe thanks to a combination of compact dimensions and entry-level pricing, and now they want to make it even more enticing with a fresh special edition. “The LBX has quickly established itself as a highly stylish leader for Lexus, (…) this new special edition will maintain the model’s reputation for distinctive good looks and authentic luxury features, matched to highly efficient and refined performance,” said Andre Schmidt, Head of Lexus Europe.
The features offered with the special edition include a new and exclusive Skylight Blue exterior color or an alternate Cement Grey bi-tone paint finish, paired with a black roof and pillars plus a jet-black treatment for elements such as the lower moldings front and back or the “resolute look” bar. There are also matte black finished 18-inch alloy wheels along with a “laser-etched-like striped pattern that creates a subtle L motif on the rear pillars.”
Moving inside, the cabin gains black semi-aniline leather upholstery with “ochre stitching along the seams and hatched embroidery across the seatbacks.” There is also highlighting stitchwork on the center console and door panels, plus a leather-wrapped steering wheel and shift lever. Additionally, Lexus adds that the special edition is based on the high specification LBX Emotion trim level.
That means the limited series comes with perks like heated front sports seats with eight-way power adjustment and memory settings, the Lexus e-Latch door operation, which is unique to the LBX in the class, plus paddle shifters for additional power control.
There is also a 12.3-inch digital instrument display for the driver, scuff plates, plus the 9.8-inch LexusLink Connect multimedia package featuring wireless smartphone integration, along with the Lexus Safety System + portfolio of active safety and driver assistance systems. Lexus announced that first deliveries are coming in early 2027.
